recentItems.title: 100,000+ Stand With Jensen Huang, NVIDIA’s Future In ‘Dark’ As Employees Want This From Board? WATCH
recentItems.description:
100,000+ Stand With Jensen Huang, NVIDIA’s Future In ‘Dark’ As Employees Want This From Board? WATCH


Though the scandal surrounding Jensen Huang continues to make headlines across the tech world, a petition to bring him back to Nvidia's top post is gaining momentum. ‘Stand With Jensen!’ Yes, that’s the name of the campaign that started after Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia's CEO. As of November 15, more than 134,000 people have signed this letter. It claims that more than 6,500 are current Nvidia employees, more than a thousand are former Nvidia employees, and over 70,000 are the company’s shareholders. Watch the video to know more details.

recentItems.title: SHOCKING! Yemen Forces Pull Back From Bab el-Mandeb! Houthis Tighten Grip On Key Maritime Chokepoint
recentItems.description:
Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces have withdrawn from the strategic Bab el-Mandeb area, leaving Iran-aligned Houthi rebels in control of the key maritime zone. The retreat gives the Houthis greater leverage over one of the world's busiest shipping routes, connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and the Suez Canal.

Megaspeed has also ordered an internal investigation.

recentItems.title: Odisha On Cyclone Alert Again? After Arnab, Murasu, 3rd Storm in 3 Weeks? Bengal Braces For Impact
recentItems.description:
Odisha is bracing for a possible third cyclone in three weeks as a low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm by Monday. With Cyclones Arnab and Murasu having recently impacted the region, authorities have alerted district collectors and activated disaster preparedness measures.

recentItems.title: 'Bukele Won't Be Alone!' Haitians Back Salvadoran Troops As Gang-Held Sylvio Cator Stadium Falls
recentItems.description:
Haitians are expressing support for El Salvador's intervention against armed gangs in Port-au-Prince, with some saying President Nayib Bukele will not stand alone if he helps restore security in Haiti. In a major development, Haitian and Salvadoran forces have taken control of the Sylvio Cator Stadium, evicting gangs that had occupied the country's main sports venue since 2024. Salvadoran soldiers are now seen patrolling the streets as residents hope for greater security and freedom of movement. Watch the latest ground report from Haiti.
